key_insight: Machine-learning optimized microwave pulses make parity-based qubit readout robust enough to improve dark-matter search sensitivity even when qubit-cavity coupling is pushed into a more error-prone regime.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that robust pulse design can trade control complexity for faster sensor cycles, enabling practical, scalable quantum hardware for microwave axion and dark-photon searches.
method: Use a transmon qubit dispersively coupled to a double-cavity system for QND photon-number readout.
Increase qubit-cavity coupling to shorten measurement cycles, while compensating detuning-induced errors with ML-optimized $c0/2$ pulses.
Combine parity-check measurement sequences with Hidden Markov Model analysis to suppress background and extract weak-signal statistics.
evidence_signal: The protocol preserves single-photon detection performance with background rates of about O(20) Hz and yields a dark-photon exclusion sensitivity of $b5_{95\%}\sim 1\times10^{-14}$ at 5.051 GHz.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful pulse optimization and operating-point calibration, since strong coupling increases detuning sensitivity and photon-number-dependent control errors.
paper_title: Benchmarking Dark Matter Search using a Parity-Check Protocol with Machine-Learning Optimized Pulses
